symptom: The synthetic claimed-anchor helper verified an Ed25519 claim against a preflighted caller policy, then read caller-owned policy.anchors again for key correlation. A descriptor proxy could substitute a different publicKeyDigest on the later read, producing a matching claimed-anchor flag for a key absent from the validated policy. The outer synthetic-reference helper repeated the same caller policy across phases. No independent authority or scoring was granted.
lesson: A full signed-request digest can remain unchanged while a caller-owned trust-policy anchor digest is swapped after mathematical signature verification. Correlating the key against a later policy graph can falsely report matching caller claims even though no real external trust exists.
guardrail: Take one bounded descriptor-only detached snapshot of caller-supplied policy before signature math and all subsequent claimed-anchor/reference comparisons. Pass that same snapshot through every phase, never reread caller-owned anchors after preflight, and keep literal independentAuthorityVerified=false and scoringAuthorized=false. Regression tests should assert the original policy is read once and that a later attempted key swap cannot produce a match.
